name: Alabama
summary: No statewide rule. Posted signs and local ordinances govern.
restArea: Rest areas are for short breaks (typically 30 min – 2 hr). Sleeping is not explicitly prohibited statewide, but local enforcement varies. Many weigh stations post 30-minute limits.
publicLand: BLM and National Forest land follow federal rules: 14-day limit, 200 ft from water. No specific state restrictions found.
cityParking: Most Alabama cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking on public streets unless explicitly permitted. Check local municipal codes.

name: Alaska
summary: Permissive on public land. Rest areas and cities have local limits.
restArea: No statewide rest-area sleeping ban. Some areas post 8-hour limits. Enforcement is limited in rural Alaska.
publicLand: Very permissive. BLM and National Forest land allow dispersed camping with 14-day federal limit. Many Alaskans live in vehicles year-round.
cityParking: Anchorage and Fairbanks have specific overnight parking restrictions in downtown areas. Rural towns are generally more lenient.

name: Arizona
summary: State trooper rest areas allow 8 hours. City rules vary widely.
restArea: Arizona State Trooper rest areas permit up to 8 hours overnight. This is among the most explicit rest-area allowances in the country.
publicLand: BLM and National Forest land follow standard federal 14-day rule. Arizona has extensive BLM land (over 7.5 million acres) making it one of the best states for dispersed camping.
cityParking: Phoenix, Tucson, and other major cities generally prohibit overnight parking. Some smaller towns are more permissive. Walmart and other businesses set their own policies.

name: Arkansas
summary: No statewide rule. BLM and forest land follow federal guidelines.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy. Individual areas may post their own limits.
publicLand: Hot Springs National Park and Ozark National Forest follow standard federal camping rules. BLM land in western Arkansas allows dispersed camping.
cityParking: Most cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking on streets. Little Rock and other urban areas enforce this.

name: California
summary: Strict urban rules. Rest areas allow up to 8 hours (Caltrans). BLM land is extensive.
restArea: Caltrans allows vehicles in rest areas for up to 8 hours before they may be removed (Caltrans Maintenance Manual, Vol. 1 Ch. 3); napping is a listed intended use. Camping is prohibited. Individual areas can post stricter limits — the posted sign governs.
publicLand: Extensive BLM (13+ million acres) and National Forest land. 14-day federal limit applies. Many areas have fire restrictions that limit camping seasons. Some BLM areas are closed to overnight stays.
cityParking: Most California cities strictly prohibit overnight vehicle parking. LA, SF, and other major cities actively enforce. Some smaller cities are more lenient.

name: Colorado
summary: Rest areas allow 8 hours. Extensive public land for dispersed camping.
restArea: Colorado state rest areas generally allow up to 8 hours overnight. Some areas are more restrictive. Signs at individual rest areas govern.
publicLand: Large BLM and National Forest areas, especially in western and southern Colorado. 14-day federal limit. Some areas have seasonal closures.
cityParking: Denver and other cities prohibit overnight parking on public streets. Colorado Springs and smaller towns vary.

name: Connecticut
summary: No statewide rule. Urban areas enforce no-overnight-parking strictly.
restArea: No explicit statewide policy. Rest areas are for short breaks.
publicLand: Limited public land. National forest areas in the south follow federal rules. Most of CT is private or state-managed.
cityParking: Most Connecticut towns and cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Enforcement is common in urban areas.

name: Delaware
summary: Small state with limited options. No specific statewide camping rules.
restArea: Limited rest areas. No explicit statewide sleeping policy.
publicLand: Very limited public land. Delaware State Forest allows camping in designated areas only.
cityParking: Most Delaware cities and towns prohibit overnight vehicle parking.

name: Florida
summary: Rest areas allow up to 8 hours. No specific statewide ban on sleeping in vehicles.
restArea: Florida rest areas generally allow up to 8 hours. Some areas post shorter limits. No statewide ban on sleeping in a parked vehicle.
publicLand: National Forest and BLM land (especially in the panhandle) follow federal 14-day rules. Many state parks prohibit vehicle camping outside designated sites.
cityParking: Most Florida cities prohibit overnight parking. Miami, Jacksonville, Tampa enforce actively. Some smaller cities are lenient.

name: Georgia
summary: Rest areas allow 8 hours. State law specifically addresses sleeping in vehicles.
restArea: Georgia state law (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-133) allows drivers to rest in vehicles at rest areas for up to 8 hours. This is one of the clearest rest-area allowances in the country.
publicLand: Chattahoochee National Forest and BLM land follow standard federal rules. 14-day limit applies.
cityParking: Most Georgia cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Atlanta, Savannah, and other cities enforce. Some smaller towns are more permissive.

name: Hawaii
summary: Strict rules. No overnight parking on most beaches and highways.
restArea: No rest areas with sleeping allowances. Hawaii does not have interstate rest areas in the traditional sense.
publicLand: National Park land (Hawai'i Volcanoes, Kilauea) follows park-specific rules. BLM land is minimal. State land generally prohibits overnight camping outside designated sites.
cityParking: Strictly enforced. Honolulu and other urban areas prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Beach parking is heavily restricted.

name: Idaho
summary: Permissive on public land. Rest areas have no explicit statewide limit.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping limit. Individual areas may post their own rules.
publicLand: Extensive BLM and National Forest land. Idaho is one of the best states for dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. Many areas are very permissive.
cityParking: Most Idaho cities prohibit overnight parking on public streets. Boise and other cities enforce. Rural areas are generally more lenient.

name: Illinois
summary: No statewide rule. Urban areas enforce no-overnight-parking.
restArea: Illinois rest areas (on interstate highways) are for short breaks. No explicit statewide sleeping allowance.
publicLand: Limited BLM land. National Forest areas (Shawnee, William T. Davis) follow federal rules. Most public land is state-managed.
cityParking: Chicago and most Illinois cities strictly prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Enforcement is common.

name: Indiana
summary: No statewide rule. Most cities prohibit overnight parking.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: Limited public land. National forest and BLM areas follow federal rules. Most of Indiana is private land.
cityParking: Most Indiana cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking on public streets.

name: Iowa
summary: No statewide rule. Limited public land for dispersed camping.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: Very limited BLM land. Some National Wildlife Refuges allow day use only. Iowa has very little land suitable for dispersed vehicle camping.
cityParking: Most Iowa cities and towns prohibit overnight vehicle parking.

name: Kansas
summary: No statewide rule. BLM land in western Kansas follows federal rules.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy. Some rest areas post their own limits.
publicLand: BLM land in western Kansas allows dispersed camping with 14-day federal limit. Eastern Kansas has very limited public land.
cityParking: Most Kansas cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Wichita, Kansas City, and Topeka enforce.

name: Kentucky
summary: No statewide rule. Limited public land options.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: Limited BLM land. National forest areas follow federal rules. Most of Kentucky is private or state-managed land.
cityParking: Most Kentucky cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking on public streets.

name: Louisiana
summary: No statewide rule. Urban areas enforce no-overnight-parking.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: Limited public land. National Wildlife Refuges and some state land allow camping in designated areas only.
cityParking: Most Louisiana cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. New Orleans, Baton Rouge enforce actively.

name: Maine
summary: Permissive on public land. Forest Service land follows federal rules.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy. Maine has few interstate rest areas.
publicLand: Forest Service land (Baxter State Park area) and some BLM land allow dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. Maine is generally permissive.
cityParking: Most Maine cities and towns prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Portland and other cities enforce.

name: District of Columbia
summary: Single municipality — no interstate rest areas. City rules and posted signs govern.
restArea: DC has no interstate highway rest areas (it is a single city). Overnight sleeping in a parked vehicle is governed by local D.C. parking rules and posted signage rather than a statewide rest-area statute.
publicLand: Very limited dispersed-camping public land within the District. The National Mall, parks, and surrounding federal land follow their own posted rules; no BLM/National Forest dispersed camping exists inside DC city limits.
cityParking: D.C. prohibits overnight parking on most streets unless explicitly permitted by signage. Residential zones (especially near parks and downtown) enforce strictly. Check the specific block's posted restrictions before leaving your vehicle.

name: Maryland
summary: No statewide rule. Urban areas (especially near DC) enforce strictly.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: Limited BLM land. National forest areas follow federal rules. Most public land is state-managed.
cityParking: Most Maryland cities and counties prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Baltimore and suburbs enforce.

name: Massachusetts
summary: Strict urban rules. No specific statewide camping law.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: Very limited public land for dispersed camping. Most is state-managed (state forests, reservations).
cityParking: Most Massachusetts cities and towns strictly prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Boston enforces actively.

name: Michigan
summary: No statewide rule. State forests and DNR land have specific camping rules.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: DNR-managed land and state forests have designated camping areas. BLM land is minimal. Dispersed camping is limited to designated areas on most state land.
cityParking: Most Michigan cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Detroit, Grand Rapids, and other cities enforce.

name: Minnesota
summary: Permissive in rural areas. DNR land follows specific camping regulations.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy. Some rest areas post 30-minute limits.
publicLand: DNR-managed land allows dispersed camping in many areas. 14-day limit on federal land. Minnesota is generally permissive for vehicle camping in rural areas.
cityParking: Most Minnesota cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Minneapolis, St. Paul enforce actively.

name: Mississippi
summary: No statewide rule. Limited public land options.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: Very limited public land for dispersed camping. National Wildlife Refuges allow day use only in most areas.
cityParking: Most Mississippi cities and towns prohibit overnight vehicle parking.

name: Missouri
summary: No statewide rule. Forest Service and state land follow specific rules.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: Mark Twain National Forest and other federal land follow standard 14-day rules. State forests have designated camping areas.
cityParking: Most Missouri cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. St. Louis, Kansas City enforce.

name: Montana
summary: Very permissive on public land. One of the best states for vanlife.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping limit. Montana is generally permissive. Individual areas may post their own rules.
publicLand: Extensive BLM and National Forest land. Montana is one of the most permissive states for dispersed vehicle camping. 14-day federal limit. Many locals and long-term vehicle dwellers.
cityParking: Most Montana cities prohibit overnight parking on public streets, but enforcement is often relaxed in smaller towns. Billings, Missoula, Bozeman vary.

name: Nebraska
summary: No statewide rule. BLM land in western Nebraska follows federal rules.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: BLM land in western Nebraska allows dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. Eastern Nebraska has very limited public land.
cityParking: Most Nebraska cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Omaha, Lincoln enforce.

name: Nevada
summary: Very permissive on public land. Rest areas allow 8 hours.
restArea: Nevada rest areas generally allow up to 8 hours overnight. State law is permissive about sleeping in vehicles in rest areas.
publicLand: Extensive BLM land (over 16 million acres — the most of any state). 14-day federal limit. Nevada is one of the best states for dispersed camping and vanlife.
cityParking: Las Vegas and Reno prohibit overnight parking on public streets. Smaller towns are generally more permissive. Some areas have specific van-friendly zones.

name: New Hampshire
summary: No statewide rule. Limited public land. Urban areas enforce no-parking.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: White Mountain National Forest follows federal rules. Limited BLM land. Most public land is state-managed.
cityParking: Most New Hampshire cities and towns prohibit overnight vehicle parking.

name: New Jersey
summary: Strict rules. No overnight parking in most urban areas.
restArea: New Jersey Turnpike rest areas are for short breaks. No explicit sleeping allowance.
publicLand: Very limited public land for dispersed camping. Most is state-managed (state forests, pinelands).
cityParking: Most New Jersey cities and towns strictly prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Enforcement is common.

name: New Mexico
summary: Permissive on public land. Extensive BLM and national forest land.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping limit. Some areas post their own rules.
publicLand: Extensive BLM and National Forest land. New Mexico is very permissive for dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. Many vanlife-friendly areas.
cityParking: Most New Mexico cities prohibit overnight parking. Albuquerque, Santa Fe enforce. Smaller towns are often more lenient.

name: New York
summary: Strict urban rules. Adirondacks have specific camping regulations.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy. Some areas post limits.
publicLand: Adirondack Park and National Forest land have specific camping rules. BLM land is minimal. 14-day federal limit where applicable.
cityParking: New York City and most cities strictly prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Enforcement is very active.

name: North Carolina
summary: No statewide rule. State parks and forests have specific camping rules.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy. Some rest areas post 30-minute limits.
publicLand: Pisgah and Nantahala National Forests follow federal rules. State forests have designated camping areas. 14-day federal limit.
cityParking: Most North Carolina cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Charlotte, Raleigh, Asheville enforce.

name: North Dakota
summary: Very permissive on public land. Sparse population means low enforcement.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping limit. North Dakota is generally permissive.
publicLand: Extensive BLM and National Forest land. Very permissive for dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. Low population means minimal enforcement pressure.
cityParking: Most North Dakota cities prohibit overnight parking, but enforcement is minimal in smaller towns. Fargo, Bismarck vary.

name: Ohio
summary: No statewide rule. Limited public land. Urban areas enforce no-parking.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: Limited BLM land. National forest areas (Cuyahoga Valley) follow federal rules. Most public land is state-managed.
cityParking: Most Ohio cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Columbus, Cleveland, Cincinnati enforce.

summary: No statewide rule. BLM land in western Oklahoma follows federal rules.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: BLM land in western Oklahoma allows dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. Eastern Oklahoma has limited public land.
cityParking: Most Oklahoma cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Oklahoma City, Tulsa enforce.

name: Oregon
summary: Permissive on public land. Rest areas allow 8 hours in many areas.
restArea: Many Oregon rest areas allow up to 8 hours overnight. Some areas are more restrictive. Check individual rest area signs.
publicLand: Extensive BLM and National Forest land. Oregon is very permissive for dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. Many vanlife-friendly areas, especially in central and eastern Oregon.
cityParking: Portland and other cities prohibit overnight parking on public streets. Smaller towns are often more permissive. Some areas have specific rules for vehicle dwelling.

name: Pennsylvania
summary: No statewide rule. State forests have specific camping regulations.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: State forests and National Forest land (Allegheny) follow specific camping rules. BLM land is minimal. 14-day federal limit where applicable.
cityParking: Most Pennsylvania cities and towns prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Philadelphia, Pittsburgh enforce.

name: Rhode Island
summary: Small state with very limited camping options. No specific statewide rules.
restArea: No rest areas with sleeping allowances.
publicLand: Very limited public land. State forests allow camping in designated areas only.
cityParking: Most Rhode Island cities and towns prohibit overnight vehicle parking.

name: South Carolina
summary: No statewide rule. State parks and forests have specific camping rules.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: National forest land (Santee, Congaree) follows federal rules. State forests have designated camping areas.
cityParking: Most South Carolina cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Charleston, Columbia enforce.

name: South Dakota
summary: Very permissive. State law specifically allows sleeping in vehicles in many situations.
restArea: South Dakota is among the most permissive states. Rest areas and highway pull-offs generally allow overnight stays. No explicit statewide time limit found.
publicLand: Extensive BLM and National Forest land (Custer, Black Hills). Very permissive for dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. South Dakota is a top state for vanlife.
cityParking: Most South Dakota cities prohibit overnight parking on public streets, but enforcement is minimal in smaller towns. Rapid City, Sioux Falls vary.

name: Tennessee
summary: No statewide rule. Great Smoky Mountains has specific camping regulations.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy. Some rest areas post limits.
publicLand: Great Smoky Mountains National Park prohibits overnight vehicle parking outside designated areas. Other National Forest land follows federal 14-day rules.
cityParking: Most Tennessee cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Nashville, Memphis, Knoxville enforce.

name: Texas
summary: Rest areas allow up to 24 hours — among the most permissive caps in the country (Tex. Transp. Code 545.411). Tents/shelters prohibited.
restArea: A full day in any rest area — among the most permissive caps (Tex. Transp. Code 545.411). Tents and shelters are prohibited, but sleeping inside a legally parked vehicle is permitted within the 24-hour cap. Individual areas may post stricter limits.
publicLand: BLM land in West Texas allows dispersed camping under the 14-day federal limit. National Forest land (Sam Houston, Davy Crockett) follows federal rules. Texas is large and rules vary enormously by region — rural counties are far more permissive than urban areas.
cityParking: Most Texas cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking on public streets. Houston, Dallas, Austin, San Antonio enforce actively. Smaller towns and rural counties vary widely — some allow it unless specifically posted against.

name: Utah
summary: Permissive on public land. Rest areas allow 8 hours. Great for dispersed camping.
restArea: Utah rest areas generally allow up to 8 hours overnight. State is permissive about sleeping in vehicles at rest areas.
publicLand: Extensive BLM and National Forest land. Utah is one of the best states for dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. Many vanlife-friendly areas, especially in the south (Moab, Capitol Reef area).
cityParking: Most Utah cities prohibit overnight parking on public streets. Salt Lake City, Provo enforce. Moab and other tourist towns are more permissive.

name: Vermont
summary: No statewide rule. Limited public land. Small towns generally permissive.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy. Vermont has few interstate rest areas.
publicLand: Green Mountain National Forest follows federal rules. Limited BLM land. Most public land is state-managed.
cityParking: Most Vermont cities and towns prohibit overnight vehicle parking, but enforcement is often relaxed in small towns.

summary: No statewide rule. State parks and forests have specific camping rules.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy. Some rest areas post limits.
publicLand: Shenandoah National Park prohibits overnight vehicle parking outside designated areas. Other National Forest land follows federal 14-day rules.
cityParking: Most Virginia cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Richmond, Virginia Beach, Norfolk enforce.

name: Washington
summary: Permissive on public land. Rest areas allow 8 hours in many areas.
restArea: Many Washington rest areas allow up to 8 hours overnight. Some areas are more restrictive. Check individual rest area signs.
publicLand: Extensive BLM and National Forest land. Washington is permissive for dispersed camping. 14-day federal limit. Olympic National Park has specific rules.
cityParking: Seattle and other cities prohibit overnight parking on public streets. Smaller towns are often more permissive. Some areas have specific rules for vehicle dwelling.

summary: No statewide rule. Limited public land. Small towns generally permissive.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: National forest land (Monongahela) follows federal rules. Limited BLM land. Most public land is state-managed.
cityParking: Most West Virginia cities and towns prohibit overnight vehicle parking, but enforcement is often relaxed.

name: Wisconsin
summary: No statewide rule. DNR land follows specific camping regulations.
restArea: No explicit statewide rest-area sleeping policy.
publicLand: DNR-managed land and National Forest areas follow specific camping rules. BLM land is minimal. 14-day federal limit where applicable.
cityParking: Most Wisconsin cities prohibit overnight vehicle parking. Milwaukee, Madison enforce.

name: Wyoming
summary: Very permissive. State law specifically addresses vehicle camping. Top state for vanlife.
restArea: Wyoming is among the most permissive states. Rest areas and highway pull-offs generally allow overnight stays. State law does not prohibit sleeping in a parked vehicle in most situations.
publicLand: Extensive BLM and National Forest land. Wyoming is arguably the most vanlife-friendly state in the country. 14-day federal limit. Very low population means minimal enforcement. Many long-term vehicle dwellers.
cityParking: Most Wyoming cities prohibit overnight parking on public streets, but enforcement is minimal. Cheyenne, Cody, Jackson vary. Many smaller towns are very permissive.
legalBasis: Wyo. Stat. § 31-6-105 (parking regulations — permissive interpretation for parked vehicles)
